newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US bond vols flat, more range-trade seen.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US bond vols flat, more range-trade seen.

text.p: Implied volatilities for options on U.S. debt futures were little changed Wednesday, implying market participants were looking for a muted reaction to late-week U.S. data, traders said.
"People don't think we're going to get any big moves," said a Eurodollar options broker at a European bank.
The underlying futures held to small ranges, with December Eurodollars ending a half basis point higher at 93.815 and September bonds finishing up 2/32 at 110-19.
May U.S. retail sales are scheduled for release Thursday, followed by the May producer price index Friday.

"We've got a really light schedule this week and technical trading should take over tomorrow," said a bond floor broker, who also said he interpreted the low volatilities to mean the market was not looking for another price breakout.
Bond futures have meandered sideways to lower since the September contract vaulted to a 3-1/2-month high on Friday in the wake of the May employment report.
In Eurodollar options, floor traders said an investment bank sold 4,000 July 94.00 straddles and a trading firm sold another 1,000 of the straddles.
Volatility was steady to slightly lower on the day, with September slipping 0.2 percentage point to 8.3 percent and December declining 0.4 point to 10.3 percent.

September Treasury bond volatility, at 8.35 percent, was unchanged from the previous day after sticking near that level for most of today's quiet session, floor brokers said. July upticked slightly to 7.80 percent, still notably low, they said.
Late in the day, a dealer firm's purchase of 3,000 July 112-00 calls and 1,000 July 111-00 calls caught the floor's attention, traders said.
